scenes.text: The famous War of the Worlds radio panic was mostly made up by newspapers.
On October thirtieth, nineteen thirty eight, Orson Welles aired a radio play about Martians landing in New Jersey.
The next morning, headlines claimed the whole country had panicked.
But a ratings survey that night found only about two percent of listeners were tuned in.
Most people were listening to a popular comedy show on another station.
Historians think newspapers hyped the story to make radio, their new rival, look dangerous.
Would you have believed the Martians were real?

title: The War of the Worlds panic was mostly a myth 👽
caption: Orson Welles' 1938 Martian radio play supposedly caused nationwide panic. In reality, few people were even listening, and historians say newspapers blew the story up to make radio look bad. 👽
